**NFLX - Netflix, Inc.**

- **Sector:** Communication Services
- **Industry:** Entertainment
- **CEO:** Theodore A. Sarandos
- **Employees:** 16000
- **Country:** US
- **Website:** https://www.netflix.com
- **IPO Date:** 2002-05-23


**Description:**
Netflix, Inc. serves as a worldwide entertainment provider. Its comprehensive library features television series, motion pictures, documentaries, and mobile games, spanning numerous genres and languages. Members can effortlessly stream this content through a variety of internet-connected devices, including smart TVs, digital media players, cable boxes, and mobile phones. Furthermore, the company continues to offer a DVD-by-mail subscription service to its customers in the United States. With roughly 222 million paying subscribers distributed across 190 countries, Netflix was founded in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.

content.text:
## Closest public peers to Netflix (NFLX)

### Most direct streaming competitors
- **The Walt Disney Company (DIS)** — Disney+, Hulu and ESPN streaming
- **Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD)** — Max
- **Paramount Skydance (PSKY)** — Paramount+ and Pluto TV
- **Comcast (CMCSA)** — NBCUniversal and Peacock
- **Amazon (AMZN)** — Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios
- **Apple (AAPL)** — Apple TV+
- **Alphabet (GOOG/GOOGL)** — YouTube and YouTube TV

### Additional video/platform peers
- **Roku (ROKU)** — streaming platform and The Roku Channel
- **Fox Corporation (FOX/FOXA)** — Tubi and traditional television assets

For a focused public-company comparable set, I would use **DIS, WBD, PSKY and CMCSA**. Amazon, Apple and Alphabet are important competitors but are much more diversified, making valuation comparisons with Netflix less clean.
